relevance_reason: Reports a CAMT patient with a homozygous THPO promoter variant, functional studies, serum THPO measurement, and response to eltrombopag.

findings.statement: Capaci et al. (2023) reported a boy born to consanguineous Muslim Palestinian parents (first cousins) who came to medical attention at 3.5 years with easy bruising and thrombocytopenia (21 x 10(9)/L) and a normal mean platelet volume. His platelet count shortly after birth was 70 x 10(9)/L. At age 2 years he had severe thrombocytopenia (20 x 10(9)/L) when diagnosed with urethral stenosis. Bone marrow examination showed normocellular marrow with severe megakaryocyte hypoplasia and mild dyserythropoiesis; aside from mild occasional neutropenia he had no other cytopenias, and Fanconi anemia was excluded by chromosomal breakage analysis.
quotes: The proband (II-3) (Figure 1A) was a 3.5-year-old boy when he presented to our hospital with easy bruising and thrombocytopenia (platelet count: 21x109/L) with a normal mean platelet volume.

Bone marrow examination from two different biopsies showed a normocellular marrow with severe hypoplasia of the megakaryocytes, with a few small immature forms seen, and mild dyserythropoiesis, consistent with amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia.
The proband was born to Muslim Palestinian parents who are first cousins to one another.

findings.statement: By whole-exome sequencing in the Palestinian boy with CAMT, Capaci et al. (2023) identified a homozygous c.-323C>T substitution (chr3:g.184096040G>A, GRCh37) in the promoter region of the THPO gene (transcript variant 1, NM_000460), 45 nucleotides upstream of the transcription start site. The parents and a younger sibling were heterozygous and two healthy siblings were homozygous wildtype; the variant was in dbSNP (rs1208732776) but not in gnomAD, and lies in a region conserved across species. No variants were found in MPL, MECOM, HOXA11, RBM8A or other bone marrow failure genes.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing allowed us to identify a homozygous nucleotide substitution (chr3:g.184096040G>A from GRCh37) within the THPO gene in the proband (Figure 1B).

Consistent with consanguinity, segregation analysis revealed that the parents and the younger sibling of the proband (II-4) were heterozygous for c.-323C>T whereas the other two healthy siblings were homozygous for the wildtype allele (Figure 1A). The variant is very rare, reported in the dbSNP (rs1208732776) but not in GnomAD.
No additional variant was detected in other genes causative of amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenias, such as MPL, MECOM, HOXA11 or RBM8A

findings.statement: Capaci et al. (2023) noted that the heterozygous mother and younger sibling of the homozygous proband had asymptomatic mild thrombocytopenia (mother around 80 x 10(9)/L, worsening during pregnancies; sibling 130 x 10(9)/L at birth), consistent with mild thrombocytopenia in carriers of monoallelic THPO loss-of-function variants.
quotes: Of interest, the proband’s mother (II-2) and one sibling (II-4), heterozygous for c.-323C>T, have asymptomatic mild thrombocytopenia, which is consistent with the slightly reduced platelet count observed in individuals with monoallelic loss-of-function variants of THPO.
His mother (I-2) has a history of mild thrombocytopenia that worsened during each pregnancy; her platelet counts are now stable around 80x109/L, and her mean platelet volume is normal.

findings.statement: Capaci et al. (2023) found that c.-323C>T lies within predicted ETS1 and STAT4 binding sites that were abolished by the variant. In luciferase assays in HEK293T cells the mutant THPO promoter reduced reporter activity by almost 80%; silencing ETS1 and/or STAT4 reduced wildtype promoter activity, and chromatin immunoprecipitation showed reduced binding of the transcription factors, at least STAT4, to the mutant promoter.
quotes: Nucleotide c.-323C was predicted to be within the consensus sequence for the binding of c-ETS-1 (here after ETS1) and STAT4 (Figure 2A).

Transfecting HEK293T cells, which constitutively express THPO, we observed that c.-323C>T significantly reduced (by almost 80%) the reporter activity as compared to the wild-type counterpart (Figure 2B).
Taken together, these data suggest that ETS1 and STAT4 are able to bind the THPO promoter and that this interaction is significantly impaired, at least for STAT4, in the presence of c.-323C>T.

findings.statement: Capaci et al. (2023) showed that knockdown of ETS1 and STAT4 in HepG2 hepatocyte cells strongly reduced endogenous THPO mRNA and protein, and that ETS1 and STAT4 interact (proximity ligation and coimmunoprecipitation), suggesting they form a transcriptional complex on THPO regulatory sequences. STAT3 knockdown also reduced THPO expression, although no STAT3 binding site was predicted in the promoter.
quotes: Knocking down ETS1 and STAT4 alone or in combination strongly reduced THPO at both mRNA and protein levels (Figure 3A, B), demonstrating that ETS1 and STAT4 regulate its endogenous expression in a hepatocyte cell model.

The interaction of the two transcription factors was confirmed by co-immunoprecipitation of the STAT4 and ETS1 proteins from lysates of HepG2 cells (Figure 3D), suggesting that they form a transcriptional complex on THPO regulatory sequences, promoting THPO transcription.

findings.statement: Capaci et al. (2023) found that the proband's serum THPO concentration was 126 pg/mL (reference 15-80 pg/mL for children), only slightly elevated despite the severely reduced megakaryocyte and platelet mass, whereas THPO levels are expected to be markedly elevated in amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia (median 1,493 pg/mL in 56 patients with CAMT due to MPL mutations). The authors suggested that a normal serum THPO in amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia should prompt suspicion of a THPO defect.
quotes: The THPO concentration was 126 pg/mL (laboratory reference range 15-80 pg/mL for children <15 years old), a value within the normal range when obtained in healthy individuals, and slightly high for children.
The finding of a normal serum THPO level in the context of an amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia should strongly suggest an alteration of THPO.

findings.statement: Capaci et al. (2023) treated the proband with eltrombopag, starting at 1.4 mg/kg/day; platelet count stabilized around 40 x 10(9)/L after 1 month, and after a dose increase to 2.8 mg/kg/day it rose gradually to 125 x 10(9)/L after 6 months, with resolution of easy bruising. This was the first report of eltrombopag therapy in a patient with a THPO mutation.
quotes: He was therefore started on eltrombopag 1.4 mg/kg/day, leading to an increase in his platelet count and then stabilization around 40x109/L after 1 month.

The patient's platelet count continues to increase gradually after 6 months of treatment at this dose; at the latest analysis, his platelet count was 125x109/L. At present, he is clinically well and no longer has easy bruising.
This is the first report of eltrombopag therapy in a patient with a THPO mutation.

relevance_reason: This paper reports a consanguineous Egyptian family with three children who have CAMT caused by a homozygous THPO mutation (p.R119C). It includes functional studies of the variant and the outcome of romiplostim treatment, so it directly establishes CAMT2.

findings.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) reported 3 sibs with congenital amegakaryocytic thrombocytopenia, born to first-cousin Egyptian parents. The proband, a boy, presented at 3.5 years of age with ecchymoses. He had very severe thrombocytopenia (platelets 3 x 10(9)/l), hyporegenerative anemia and severe neutropenia. Bone marrow was hypocellular with very rare immature megakaryocytes and a normal karyotype. He also had preauricular skin tags and a left divergent squint. He was initially diagnosed with idiopathic aplastic anemia, after Fanconi anemia and PNH were excluded. He went on to have recurrent major hemorrhages and severe infections that required multiple transfusions.
quotes: The propositus is a male born to first cousin parents of Egyptian origin who presented in July 2009, at the age of 3.5 years, with ecchymotic patches. His physical examination showed pre‐auricular skin tags and left eye divergent squint.
Blood cell count revealed very severe thrombocytopenia, hyporegenerative anemia (reticulocyte count 22.8 × 109/l), and severe neutropenia (Table 1).
Bone marrow examination showed hypocellularity with very rare immature megakaryocytes, and conventional marrow cytogenetics showed normal karyotype.

findings.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) found that the proband's brother had severe isolated thrombocytopenia (26 x 10(9)/l) at 7 months of age, with markedly reduced bone marrow megakaryocytes. He developed recurrent spontaneous bleeding at 1.6 years. A younger sister developed a hematoma at a vaccination site at 2 months of age and was found to have anemia and severe thrombocytopenia. Platelet size and blood cell morphology were normal. The authors noted that the oldest sib had trilineage hypoplasia, which suggested that the hematologic picture worsens with age, and that the phenotype was indistinguishable from CAMT caused by MPL mutations.
quotes: severe isolated thrombocytopenia was found in the 7‐month‐old brother (Table 1). In this subject, peripheral blood cell morphology was normal and bone marrow examination showed a remarkably decreased number of megakaryocytes without other significant abnormalities.
At the age of 2 months, she developed a hematoma at the site of vaccination. Blood cell counts revealed anemia and severe thrombocytopenia with normal blood cell morphology.

However, the trilineage aplasia observed in the oldest sibling suggests that the hematological picture worsens with age. As a matter of fact, the clinical presentation of these patients appears indistinguishable from that of subjects with CAMT due to MPL mutations.

findings.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) sequenced MPL and THPO in the proband and found no MPL variants. They identified a homozygous c.355C>T variant in THPO (p.R119C). The variant segregated with the disease: both affected sibs were homozygous and the parents were heterozygous. It was absent from the dbSNP, 1000 Genomes and ExAC databases, and most in silico tools predicted it to be pathogenic.
quotes: While no variants were found in MPL, we identified the homozygous c.355C>T variant in THPO (p.R119C). Consistent with recessive inheritance of the phenotype, the proband's siblings were homozygous and the parents were heterozygous for the variant (Fig EV1).
The p.R119C is not reported in the SNP (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/SNP), 1000 Genome (1000genomes.org), and ExAC (exac.broadinstitute.org) databases.

findings.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) studied the R119C mutant in transfected HEK293T cells. It was expressed at levels similar to or higher than wildtype and was equally stable, but its concentration in culture supernatants was about 23-fold lower, indicating impaired secretion. When tested at equal concentrations, the mutant had about 50% of wildtype activity in stimulating proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells and in activating STAT5, ERK1/2 and AKT. The previously reported R38C mutant behaved similarly.
quotes: the THPO concentration in the conditioned media containing both mutants was much lower than that in the wild‐type sample (about 23‐fold lower for both the p.R119C and the p.R38C) (Table 3).
The mean activity of the p.R119C was 52% ± 7 (P < 0.05), 53% ± 9 (P < 0.05), and 45% ± 4 (P < 0.005) of the wild‐type THPO, respectively. Similar results were obtained with the p.R38C mutant (Fig 5).
The analysis confirmed that both p.R119C and p.R38C THPO induce defective activation of all the investigated intracellular signaling kinases (Fig 6A and B).

findings.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) found normal serum THPO levels in the 2 older affected sibs before treatment: 10.9 pg/ml in the proband and 14.1 pg/ml in his brother, compared with 6.9 to 54.4 pg/ml in controls. Serum THPO is markedly elevated in other forms of marrow aplasia, including MPL-related CAMT, so these levels were inappropriately low. The authors suggested that measuring serum THPO could help distinguish THPO-related CAMT from MPL-related CAMT.
quotes: In particular, THPO concentration was 10.9 pg/ml in the proband and 14.1 pg/ml in his brother. The serum THPO levels obtained in 50 consecutive healthy subjects ranged from 6.9 to 54.4 pg/ml (mean: 14.6) (Noris et al, 2011).

These observations suggest that measurement of the serum THPO level could be useful to discriminate CAMT patients with THPO mutations from those with MPL variants or other bone marrow failure syndromes.

findings.statement: Pecci et al. (2018) reported that the proband had not responded to cyclosporine A or oxymetholone. He was started on romiplostim at 4.4 years of age and showed a rapid trilineage response, with no further bleeding, infections or transfusions over 6.5 years of follow-up. Both sibs also responded to romiplostim. The brother achieved platelet counts of 30 to 100 x 10(9)/l and transfusion independence over 6.3 years. The authors noted that hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is not expected to be effective in patients with THPO mutations.
quotes: Most importantly, no further spontaneous bleeding events and infectious episodes were recorded and no further transfusion needed during romiplostim administration. The patient is currently on treatment, and the hematological and clinical response is maintained after a follow‐up of 6.5 years.
He achieved good platelet response (platelet count between 30 and 100 × 109/l) and remission of bleedings with stable independence from transfusions that was maintained after a 6.3‐year follow‐up.
Although HSCT is the cornerstone of treatment for these forms, transplantation is not expected to be effective in subjects with cytopenias deriving from defects in THPO.

relevance_reason: Reports patients with biallelic THPO mutations causing thrombocytopenia progressing to bone marrow failure that does not respond to transplant, which is the defining report for CAMT2.

findings.statement: Seo et al. (2017) reported 5 individuals from 3 unrelated families with severe thrombocytopenia that progressed to trilineage bone marrow failure. Four of the children received hematopoietic stem cell transplants. All 4 had poor graft function and persistent severe cytopenias, even after repeated transplants from different donors.
quotes: We report 5 individuals in 3 unrelated families with severe thrombocytopenia progressing to trilineage bone marrow failure (BMF).
Four of the children received hematopoietic stem cell transplants and all showed poor graft function with persistent severe cytopenias even after repeated transplants with different donors.

findings.statement: Seo et al. (2017) used exome and targeted sequencing to identify a homozygous R99W mutation in the THPO gene in affected children from 2 of the 3 families with thrombocytopenia progressing to bone marrow failure. The mutation resulted in a lack of THPO in the patients' serum.
quotes: Exome and targeted sequencing identified mutations in the gene encoding thrombopoietin (THPO): THPO R99W, homozygous in affected children in 2 families
Both mutations result in a lack of THPO in the patients' serum.

findings.statement: Seo et al. (2017) identified a homozygous R157X nonsense mutation in the THPO gene in the affected child in a third family with thrombocytopenia progressing to bone marrow failure. The patient had no THPO in the serum.
quotes: THPO R157X, homozygous in the affected child in the third family
Both mutations result in a lack of THPO in the patients' serum.

findings.statement: Seo et al. (2017) concluded that biallelic loss-of-function mutations in THPO cause bone marrow failure. They proposed that the bone marrow failure does not respond to transplant because the mechanism lies outside the hematopoietic cells. They stated that this supports the critical role of the MPL-THPO pathway in hematopoiesis.
quotes: These studies demonstrate that biallelic loss-of-function mutations in THPO cause BMF, which is unresponsive to transplant due to a hematopoietic cell-extrinsic mechanism.

findings.statement: Seo et al. (2017) found that THPO was absent from the serum of patients carrying either the R99W or the R157X mutation.
quotes: Both mutations result in a lack of THPO in the patients' serum.

findings.statement: Seo et al. (2017) reported that the 2 surviving patients showed improvement in trilineage hematopoiesis after treatment with a THPO receptor agonist.
quotes: For the 2 surviving patients, improvement in trilineage hematopoiesis was achieved following treatment with a THPO receptor agonist.

relevance_reason: Reports a homozygous THPO missense mutation causing autosomal recessive aplastic anemia in a Micronesian family, with functional evidence and heterozygous thrombocytopenia.

findings.statement: Dasouki et al. (2013) reported 2 siblings from a Micronesian family with idiopathic autosomal recessive aplastic anemia. Both parents and a sibling who were heterozygous carriers had reduced platelet counts, whereas a sibling with wildtype sequence had a normal platelet count.
quotes: We recently identified 2 siblings afflicted with idiopathic, autosomal recessive aplastic anemia.
Both parents and a sibling with heterozygous R17C change have reduced platelet counts, whereas a sibling with wild-type sequence has normal platelet count.

phenotypes.text: reduced platelet count in heterozygous carriers

findings.statement: In 2 Micronesian sibs with autosomal recessive aplastic anemia, Dasouki et al. (2013) identified by whole-exome sequencing a homozygous c.112C>T mutation in the THPO gene, resulting in an arg38-to-cys (R38C) substitution, or R17C excluding the 21-amino acid signal peptide, in the receptor-binding domain. In silico modeling predicted that the introduced fifth cysteine may disrupt normal disulfide bonding among the 4 conserved RBD cysteines and impair receptor binding. Mutant THPO-containing media showed a 2- to 3-fold reduced ability to sustain proliferation of THPO-dependent UT7-TPO cells, and the authors concluded that R17C is a partial loss-of-function allele causing aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state.
quotes: Whole-exome sequencing identified a novel homozygous missense mutation in thrombopoietin (THPO, c.112C>T) in both affected siblings.
This mutation encodes an arginine to cysteine substitution at residue 38 or residue 17 excluding the 21-amino acid signal peptide of THPO receptor binding domain (RBD).
In functional assays, the mutant-THPO-containing media shows two- to threefold reduced ability to sustain UT7-TPO cells, which require THPO for proliferation.

findings.statement: Dasouki et al. (2013) found that the THPO R17C partial loss-of-function allele resulted in aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state in their family.
quotes: Thus, the R17C partial loss-of-function allele results in aplastic anemia in the homozygous state and mild thrombocytopenia in the heterozygous state in our family.
